anomaly_signals.detail: 218 genai_tool_failures recorded across 487 spans — a ~44.8% tool failure rate. This is the primary driver of the tool_meltdown scenario.
601 errors out of 1000 spans — 60.1% error rate. Likely cascading upstream failures from tool-executor and agent-service.
253 errors out of 1000 spans — 25.3% error rate. Elevated alongside postgres-auth (116/1000, 11.6%), suggesting auth pipeline instability.
219 errors out of 470 spans — 46.6% error rate. Agent orchestration is heavily impacted, consistent with tool meltdown causing agent-level failures.
121 errors out of 409 spans — 29.6% error rate, with postgres-payments also at 75/409 (18.3%). Payment flows are significantly disrupted.
p99 latency at 25,015ms (~25s) across the batch. LLM calls are likely timing out or stalling due to tool response failures feeding back into LLM retry loops.
27 genai_token_truncations detected. Likely caused by oversized retry payloads or error context being stuffed into prompts during tool failure recovery.
100 errors out of 470 spans — 21.3% error rate. Memory retrieval failures may be compounding agent decision errors.

recommended_action: Immediately investigate and halt the tool_meltdown scenario: circuit-break the tool-executor to stop cascading failures into agent-service and api-gateway. Inspect tool-executor logs for root cause (misconfigured tools, external API outages, or resource exhaustion). Simultaneously check auth-service and payments-service for downstream blast radius. Review LLM prompt construction logic to prevent error context from causing token truncations during retries.
summary: A confirmed tool_meltdown scenario is active, with 218 GenAI tool failures (~44.8% of tool-executor spans) cascading into a system-wide 24% error rate and a catastrophic p99 latency of ~25 seconds. The api-gateway (60% errors), agent-service (46.6%), payments-service (29.6%), and auth-service (25.3%) are all critically impacted, indicating broad blast radius across the entire application stack.
